'''Szymon Suckewer''' (born April 10, 1938, in Warsaw) is a Polish-born American physicist, and professor emeritus at [[Princeton University]]. His primary fields of interest include [[X-ray laser]]s, and [[X-ray microscope|X-ray microscopy]], particularly the generation of ultrashort laser pulses which are applied in [[plasma diagnostics]].

Suckewer completed his degree in physics at the [[Moscow State University|Lomonosov Moscow State University]] in 1962. He went on to receive a doctorate in physics from the Institute for Nuclear Research at the [[University of Warsaw]] in 1966. Suckewer received his habilitation in 1971 after which he was a lecturer at the Institute for Nuclear Research in Warsaw until 1975. In the same year, he went to [[Princeton University]] where he was the Senior Research Physicist in the Laboratory for Plasma Physics. From 1987 he worked as a professor and leader of a research team tasked to discover lasers with wavelengths of under 30 [[Nanometre|nm]].

In 1984 Suckewer's team succeeded in creating a laser with a wavelength of 18.2&nbsp;nm in plasma composed of carbon ions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Suckewer|first1=S.|last2=Skinner|first2=C. H.|date=1990-03-30|title=Soft x-ray lasers and their applications|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.2321016|journal=Science|language=en|volume=247|issue=4950|pages=1553–1557|doi=10.1126/science.2321016|issn=0036-8075|pmid=2321016|url-access=subscription}}</ref> This was the first successful demonstration of laser operation in the soft X-ray range, almost at the same time as Peter Hagelstein's group at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] succeeded in doing so too. For the next years, he tasked himself with the need for developing laser pulses of shorter wavelengths and inventing new techniques for producing high-intensity laser pulses.
	
In 1987 he managed to create ultrashort laser pulses within intensities of  <math display="inline">2 \times 10^{18} </math> ''<math>W \times cm^{-2}</math>'' with a [[Krypton fluoride laser|krypton-fluoride laser]]. With these pulses he managed to induce laser activity in lithium-ion plasma with wavelengths of 13.5&nbsp;nm.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Korobkin|first1=D. V.|last2=Nam|first2=C. H.|last3=Suckewer|first3=S.|last4=Goltsov|first4=A.|date=1996-12-23|title=Demonstration of Soft X-Ray Lasing to Ground State in Li III|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.5206|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=77|issue=26|pages=5206–5209|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.5206|pmid=10062742|bibcode=1996PhRvL..77.5206K |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He continued working with laser pulses of even shorter wavelengths into the 21st century. This led Suckewer to investigate applications of his lasers in fields such as bioengineering. He applied his laser technologies in the carrying out of incision-free eye surgery as well as using high-intensity lasers in the safe and efficient removal of tattoos.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alexander Smits and Szymon Suckewer: New laser method could make tattoo removal safe and effective|url=https://innovation.princeton.edu/news/alexander-smits-and-szymon-suckewer-new-laser-method-could-make-tattoo-removal-safe-and|access-date=2020-07-12|website=Princeton Innovation|language=en}}</ref>

In 1990 he received the American Physical Society's Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research. In 2005 Suckewer was presented the Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Presentation of the 2005 Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics|url=https://www.lambaward.org/2005/presentation/index.html|access-date=2020-07-12|website=www.lambaward.org}}</ref> In 2007 he received the Arthur L. Schawlow Award f''or pioneering contributions to the generation of ultra-short wavelength and femtosecond lasers and X-ray laser microscopy''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2018 Stanley Corrsin Award Recipient|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|access-date=2020-07-12|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref>

Suckewer is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]] and holds numerous patents in [[United States Patent and Trademark Office|The United States Patent and Trademark Office]]. He transferred to [[professor emeritus]] status on July 1, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Szymon Suckewer {{!}} Dean of the Faculty|url=https://dof.princeton.edu/about/clerk-faculty/emeritus/szymon-suckewer|access-date=2020-07-12|website=dof.princeton.edu}}</ref>
